sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: How did Bradley Cooper prepare for his role?

factBeats.text: Before acting, Bradley Cooper worked as a busboy, waiter, and prep cook in various restaurants.
He once cut and cleaned 620 chickens and nine boxes of peppers in a single day as a prep cook.
For the film, Cooper trained with Claire Smythe, executive chef of London’s three-Michelin-star Restaurant Gordon Ramsay.
Cooper insisted on performing all cooking scenes himself, with no stunt doubles or insert shots of other people's hands.

factBeats.text: The film's kitchen was a fully functioning set, built specifically for the movie to replicate a real restaurant environment.
To enhance authenticity, all food preparation scenes during filming were done for real, complete with active kitchen hazards.
Consultant chef Marcus Wareing even turned the stoves on full during filming to make the actors genuinely hot and sweaty.
Wareing also taught the core actors, including Adam Jones and Helene, how to cook and move like professional chefs.
To further immerse the cast, genuine chefs were hired to play minor roles in the cooking scenes.
